sources.name: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.role: provenance Entity/Activity/Agent, derivation, attribution, association and generation relation contract
verified_facts: PROV-O is the OWL 2 encoding of the PROV Data Model for interoperable provenance interchange.
It defines classes, properties and restrictions for representing provenance generated by different systems and contexts.
PROV-O can describe entities, activities, agents and qualified provenance relations.
semantic_limits: A syntactically valid PROV-O graph records asserted provenance relations; it does not independently establish that the assertions are true.
Attribution, derivation or generation links do not prove exact source bytes, complete download, authoritative cadastral identity or numeric accuracy.
Provenance metadata must not create a parcel-height row without pinned objects, digests, exact polygon, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and execution receipts.

sources.name: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.role: RDF data-graph validation against shapes, targets, focus nodes, constraints, severity and validation-report contract
verified_facts: SHACL describes and constrains RDF graphs using node shapes, property shapes and constraint components.
Targets select focus nodes and validation evaluates those focus nodes against the applicable shapes.
Validation produces a report whose conforms value summarizes whether validation results were produced.
semantic_limits: A SHACL conforms result proves conformance to the supplied shapes and data graph, not real-world truth or source authority.
Validation quality is bounded by the completeness and correctness of the shapes, targets, entailment regime and input graph.
A passing shape must not become parcel-height evidence without exact source bytes, geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units, sampling method and receipts.

sources.name: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language — Document Overview
sources.role: ontology classes, properties, individuals, axioms, profiles and formal-semantics inference contract
verified_facts: OWL 2 is an ontology language with formally defined meaning for classes, properties, individuals and data values.
OWL 2 ontologies can be exchanged as RDF documents and used with RDF data.
OWL 2 provides several profiles and semantics intended for different reasoning and implementation needs.
semantic_limits: An OWL 2 entailment follows from the selected ontology and semantics; it does not prove that asserted premises match the physical world.
Ontology consistency or successful reasoning does not establish source bytes, cadastral authority, geometry completeness or measurement accuracy.
Inferred classifications and relations must not create business rows without independent source, datum, unit, method, digest and execution evidence.

sources.name: RDF Schema 1.1
sources.role: RDF class/property, domain, range, type, subclass and subproperty vocabulary contract
verified_facts: RDF Schema provides a data-modelling vocabulary extending the basic RDF vocabulary.
It defines resources such as classes and properties plus domain, range, type, subclass and subproperty terms.
Domain and range statements support RDF entailments about the classes of subjects and objects.
semantic_limits: RDFS domain and range are inference rules, not closed-world validation constraints on every property value.
Subclass or type entailment does not authenticate the described resource or prove the correctness of numeric values.
RDFS vocabulary conformance must not substitute for exact source bytes, HMLR polygon binding, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and receipts.
